title: Microsoft Teams to get support for third-party deepfake detection tools
key_facts: New entries on the Microsoft 365 Roadmap show Microsoft is developing support for third-party deepfake detection and impersonation protection in Teams meetings.
Both are due for general availability in November after a worldwide rollout.

Certified third-party providers will analyse meeting audio and video for signs of synthetic or manipulated media and send detection signals to Teams, which will show in-meeting experiences and controls.
A separate impersonation-protection feature will warn users about suspected deceptive organisers or participants with warnings and risk indicators.
These are part of a series of Teams security additions, including QR-code blurring for external senders and blocking external bots.
quote_evidence: Organizations can enhance meeting security with synthetic audio and video detection solutions provided by certified third-party providers,

When Teams detects a potential impersonation attempt, it surfaces warnings and risk indicators to help users recognize suspicious identities and make more informed decisions when joining or participating in a meeting,
why_it_matters_hint: Microsoft plans to let companies plug deepfake detectors into video meetings and to warn users about impersonators, aimed at fraud using fake faces and voices.
event_date: Roadmap entries reported 8 Oct 2026; release planned November 2026
notes: Based on Microsoft 365 Roadmap entries as read by BleepingComputer; roadmap items can change. The Microsoft entries were not opened.
